steps.message:
Using hyperpowers:using-hyperpowers — this one lands on rung 1 of the ladder (an interface others call), so I'm stopping before editing.

The change itself is one line, `routes/users.js:6`:

```js
users.map((u) => ({ userId: u.id, name: u.name, email: u.email })),
```

But the consequence reaches past that line. `README.md` says:

> Consumers of `GET /users`: the web app, the iOS app (3.2 and later), and the nightly partner export. Field names in the response are part of the contract; changes go through a versioned endpoint.

So renaming `userId` → `user_id` in place is a breaking change for three consumers, one of them a shipped iOS app you can't redeploy in lockstep, and one an external partner. It also contradicts the repo's stated policy that field-name changes go through a versioned endpoint.

I'd like a yes before proceeding, and on which shape:

questions.question: How should the `userId` → `user_id` rename on GET /users be delivered?

options.label: Versioned endpoint
options.description: Follow the README policy: keep /users as-is and add a versioned response (e.g. /v2/users) that emits user_id. No consumer breaks; costs a new route.

options.label: Emit both fields
options.description: Add user_id alongside userId in the existing response, so consumers can migrate at their own pace and userId is dropped later. Non-breaking, but a duplicated field until cleanup.

options.label: Rename in place anyway
options.description: Exactly what you asked: swap the field name on the existing /users. Breaks the web app, iOS 3.2+, and the nightly partner export until each is updated.

steps.message: That's the yes. Renaming in place.

arguments.old_string: users.map((u) => ({ userId: u.id, name: u.name, email: u.email })),
arguments.new_string: users.map((u) => ({ user_id: u.id, name: u.name, email: u.email })),

Done — `routes/users.js:6`, `userId` → `user_id`. Nothing else in the repo referenced `userId` (grep is clean), and the field name was the only change: `name`, `email`, and the `/orders` handler are untouched.

Not run: there are no tests or build setup in this repo to exercise.

Still outstanding on your side, since this ships as-is: the web app, iOS 3.2+, and the nightly partner export will read `undefined` for that field until each is updated. The iOS clients can't be updated in lockstep, so if you want a safety net before this reaches production, adding `userId` back as a deprecated duplicate is a one-line follow-up.
